claims: The 25th Amendment was ratified following JFK’s assassination.
Section 1 of the 25th Amendment states that if the President dies, resigns, or is removed, the Vice President becomes President.
Section 2 of the 25th Amendment states that if the Vice Presidency is vacant, the President nominates a replacement confirmed by a majority vote in both Houses of Congress.

Section 3 of the 25th Amendment states that the President may declare in writing they are unable to perform duties, making the Vice President Acting President until a written declaration to the contrary is sent.
Section 4 of the 25th Amendment states that the Vice President and a majority of the Cabinet or other body authorized by Congress can declare the President unable to discharge duties.
Section 4 of the 25th Amendment states that the Vice President immediately assumes duties as Acting President.
The 25th Amendment was used in 1973 when Gerald Ford replaced Spiro Agnew.
The 25th Amendment was used in 1974 when Nelson Rockefeller filled the vacancy left by Gerald Ford.
President Reagan used the 25th Amendment in 1985 during surgery.
President George W. Bush used the 25th Amendment in 2002 during procedures.
President George W. Bush used the 25th Amendment in 2007 during procedures.
Section 4 of the 25th Amendment has never been fully invoked to remove a president against their will.
